Toy Story has basically been doing the same thing over and over again, but this time, at last, it’s a story about everyone accepting the impermanence of all things. And that made me think once again about the awkwardness of toys as a form of existence. They imitate living things, which are themselves even more impermanent, yet unlike living things, toys cannot be born and disappear with such natural fluidity. And perhaps it’s not just toys. Tables, sofas, clocks, computers, and even the information inside those computers—all of these things might be awkward, melancholy creations that human beings have made in order to forget about impermanence.

الجزء الثالث أعجبني أكثر من ناحية التوسع، وأشعر أنه أخذ عالم قصة لعبة إلى مستوى أكبر، خصوصًا مع الشخصيات والمكان الجديد. كما أن الجانب الدرامي هنا كان أقوى من الجزء الثاني بالنسبة لي، وفيه مشاعر أكثر ومواضيع أنضج. التجربة بشكل عام كانت جيدة جدًا، وأعجبني كيف حافظ الفيلم على روح السلسلة مع إعطائها مساحة أكبر للتطور. جزء ثالث ناجح؛ أكبر من السابقين، وأكثر نضجًا من ناحية المشاعر، دون أن يفقد روح السلسلة. Toy Story 3 impressed me more in terms of how much the world expands. It takes the franchise into a bigger setting with new characters and situations, while the emotional side felt stronger to me than in the second film. Overall, it was a very good experience, and I liked how it managed to keep the spirit of the franchise while allowing it to grow and become more mature. A successful third chapter—bigger than its predecessors, more emotionally mature, yet still true to the spirit of the series.
